hook: What to teach a five year old before they see something upsetting online
book_line: When screens make you sad. A few minutes, on the sofa.

ask1: Where do YOU feel a wobbly feeling? Point to it.
ask2: If a screen ever gives you the uh oh feeling, you can always come to me. You will never be in trouble.

child.text: Hello, it's Didgee. And here's Pebble.
Oh, Pebble. Other way round. Lovely.
Let's breathe together. Breathe in, and blow out slowly. One more. Lovely.
Last time, we sent a kind message. Today, we're talking about feelings.
Today's special word is feeling.
Happy, sad, excited, worried. All feelings are okay.
Most of the time, screens are fun. Songs, and games, and stories.
But sometimes, something on a screen gives you an uh oh feeling. It might be sad, or scary, or it just feels wrong.
You might feel it in your body. A wobbly tummy. A hot face. A heart going fast.
That's your body saying uh oh.
Pause me here. Where do you feel a wobbly feeling? Point to it.
When you get the uh oh feeling, here's what to do. First, turn it over.
Put the screen face down. Now you can't see it.
Then, go and tell. Find your grown up, and tell them what you saw.
Turn it over. Go and tell!
Let's play the high five game. When your grown up says uh oh, turn your hands over like a screen. Then run to them, and high five!
Ready? Uh oh!
Pause me here. Grown up, you have something important to say.
You will never be in trouble for telling. Even if you were watching something you weren't meant to. Telling is always the right thing.
When you tell, the uh oh feeling gets smaller. Your grown up helps you carry it.
So. Notice the uh oh feeling. Turn it over. Go and tell!
Tonight, play the high five game with your grown up.
Goodbye from Didgee. See you next time.

parent.text: One day, your child will see something on a screen that upsets them.

parent.big: If telling costs them the tablet, they may stop telling.
parent.text: If telling you costs them the tablet, they may stop telling you.
So make telling the easy part. Their film teaches one routine: turn it over, go and tell.
When they come to you, start with: thank you for telling me.
Then: you're not in trouble. Even if they were somewhere they shouldn't have been. Stay calm, and listen.
Their film is a few minutes on the sofa. In Guided Childhood, you can book a time to watch it together.
And if what they saw worries you, you don't have to handle it alone. The NSPCC helpline is oh eight oh eight, eight hundred, five thousand.
parent.cap: And if what they saw worries you, you don't have to handle it alone. NSPCC helpline: 0808 800 5000.
